description: Brand identity and AI image-asset generation for the Unicorn Commander suite. Lists brands, reads a brand identity, composes prompts, generates assets, browses the asset catalog, and bootstraps new brand kits.

tools.name: list_brands
tools.description: List the brand slugs seeded under the brand kits directory.

tools.name: get_brand
tools.description: Get one brand's identity: colors, fonts, voice, tagline, and references.

tools.name: list_asset_types
tools.description: List the asset-type registry. Each entry has key, label, size, default_backend, and transparent.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List the locked, data-driven layout templates the Studio renders on-brand from any brand's tokens. A template is not an image and no backend is called: each entry has an id, label, the catalog asset_type a saved render maps to, the pixel width and height, a background (brand-gradient or a solid color token), and slots positioned by 0..1 fractions of the canvas. Every color is a brand token name (brand/primary, text/foreground, and so on), never raw hex, so the render is on brand by construction. The same set GET /api/templates serves.

tools.name: build_prompt
tools.description: Compose the image prompt for a brand asset without generating anything. A dry run through the same engine live generation uses. No backend is called and no spend occurs.

asset.description: Asset type key, for example og_image.

variant.description: Optional variant name allowed by the asset's prompt template.

topic.description: Optional topic, used by text-heavy assets like og_image.

platform.description: Optional platform hint, used by social_card.

backend.description: Optional backend override: gemini, openai, recraft, or flux.

tools.name: list_generated_assets
tools.description: List previously generated assets from the on-disk catalog by reading the sidecar JSON records next to each generated image.

brand.description: Optional brand slug to restrict the listing to one brand.

asset.description: Optional asset-type key to restrict the listing to one type.

tools.name: generate_asset
tools.description: Generate a brand asset and persist it with a sidecar catalog record. Routes through the same engine the CLI and REST API use. Returns needs_key when the chosen backend has no credentials configured.

asset.description: Asset type key, for example og_image.

variant.description: Optional variant name allowed by the asset's prompt template.

topic.description: Optional topic, used by text-heavy assets like og_image.

platform.description: Optional platform hint, used by social_card.

backend.description: Optional backend override: gemini, openai, recraft, or flux.

tools.name: generate_brand_kit
tools.description: Generate a whole on-brand asset kit for a brand in one call: the batch form of generate_asset. Resolves a set of asset types and generates one of each through the same engine, so every image is on brand by construction and compliance-stamped on save. Targeting: an explicit asset_types list generates exactly those; otherwise only_missing true (the default) generates only the types the brand has no covering asset of yet (computed from the same catalog GET /api/assets reads, where a type is covered when it has an asset whose lifecycle_status is not needs_review or archived); otherwise all registry asset types. Each type is fault-isolated: a per-type failure (a backend error or a missing key) is captured with status error and never aborts the rest of the kit. Returns the brand, a results list (per type: asset_type and status ok or error, plus file, url, and the compliance summary on ok), and the generated and failed counts.

only_missing.description: When true (default) and no explicit asset_types are given, target only the asset types with no covering asset yet. Ignored when asset_types is provided.

asset_types.description: Optional explicit list of asset-type keys to generate, for example ["logo", "og_image"]. Overrides only_missing.

tools.name: generate_card
tools.description: Compose a text-bearing card (og_image or social_card) deterministically. Unlike generate_asset, the text is rendered with the brand's real fonts and exact colors over a brand background with the mark composited in, so the copy is always correct and on brand: no model text rendering, no provider key, no cost (this writes a catalog asset locally; it does not call the metered gateway). Saves into the same catalog as generate_asset (shows in the GUI, gets a compliance stamp).

message.description: Main copy (headline for og_image, tagline for social_card). Defaults to the brand tagline.

mark.description: Optional mark to composite: an absolute path, or a filename under the brand's generated/imported logo dir. Defaults to the brand's declared mark, else its most recent logo.

variant.description: Optional variant label recorded on the asset.

tools.name: new_brand
tools.description: Bootstrap a new brand kit from the blank template. Copies the template to a new brand directory and replaces the placeholder tokens with the supplied slug, display name, and optional parent slug.

slug.description: Filesystem-safe identifier for the new brand, for example majiks-studio.

display_name.description: Human-readable brand name, for example Majiks Studio.

parent.description: Optional parent brand slug if this is a sub-brand.

tools.name: clone_brand
tools.description: Clone an existing brand into a new sub-brand or a distinct seeded brand. Writes a new brand kit from the source. When as_child is true (the default) the new brand is a minimal child that inherits the source's visual and voice through the loader's parent merge; when false the source's resolved visual, voice, and prompt templates are copied in with no parent. The source's canonical mark is never copied, so the new brand starts with no logo.

slug.description: The existing source brand to clone, for example magic-unicorn.

new_slug.description: The new brand's identifier (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens), for example magic-unicorn-labs.

display_name.description: Human-readable name for the new brand.

as_child.description: True (default) inherits the source via the parent merge; false copies the source's visual, voice, and prompts in with no parent.

tools.name: intake_brand
tools.description: Draft a brand identity with the Director and create the brand. From a brand name and whatever you can say about it, the Director drafts a full identity (palette, typography, voice, style keywords, tagline, description) and a complete, valid brand kit is written from it. The slug is derived from the name. When parent is set the draft is kept consistent with the parent's palette and voice and the new brand records the parent. mode=onboard with a url drafts from the url and name as hints and notes that deep live-site capture needs Brigade. When the LLM gateway is unavailable or returns an unusable draft, a neutral on-theme default identity is written instead and a note says it is a starting point to refine. Returns the created brand, the draft, and notes.

name.description: The new brand's display name, for example Majiks Studio.

description.description: What you can say about the brand, if anything.

url.description: A related URL or the brand's live site, if any.

parent.description: An existing brand slug if this is a sub-brand.

mode.description: describe drafts from the name and description (the default); onboard drafts from the url and name as hints.

tools.name: get_brand_tokens
tools.description: Get a brand's machine-readable design tokens: semantic color tokens (brand/primary, surface/background, and so on) with hex and rgb, font tokens, and a ready-to-paste CSS custom-properties block. The portable, machine-readable form of the brand identity for agents and downstream tools.

slug.description: The brand slug, for example magic-unicorn.

tools.name: get_brand_rules
tools.description: Get a brand's deterministic compliance rules manifest: the allowed color palette, the color tolerance and gradient axis the color check uses, banned terms, required terms, voice tone, and manual review rules. This is the brand truth that agents and the rest of the suite check assets against before approving them.

slug.description: The brand slug, for example magic-unicorn.

tools.name: get_brand_guidelines
tools.description: Get a brand's full guidelines document: the assembled brand book. One read-only call returning the brand identity (slug, display name, tagline, description, parent, mark URL), the design tokens (colors with hex and rgb, plus typography), the deterministic rules manifest, the voice (tone and forbidden phrases), the logo section (mark URL and logo lockups), and every catalog asset grouped by type in the asset-type registry order with its label and count. Lets agents and other suite modules read one consistent brand book.

slug.description: The brand slug, for example magic-unicorn.

tools.name: get_share_preview
tools.description: Get a brand's social-share / link-preview kit (Open Graph + Twitter Card tags). Returns the meta tags and a ready-to-paste html snippet a brand drops into its own site's head so a shared link unfurls into the brand's 1200x630 share image. Pass canonical_url and image_url (or set the brand's website) for absolute tags; any tag left on an example domain is named in placeholders. image references the brand's og_image in the catalog, or is null if none has been generated yet.

slug.description: The brand slug, for example magic-unicorn.

canonical_url.description: The brand's site URL the shared link points to. Optional.

image_url.description: Where the brand hosts its share image. Optional.

tools.name: check_compliance
tools.description: Check an asset or a piece of text against a brand's deterministic rules and return a structured pass, warn, or fail result with a score, per-rule checks, and human-readable violations. Pass a catalog file (with its asset type and kind) to run the color-palette check on the image, or pass text to run the banned-term, em-dash, and required-term checks. No model is used; the result is deterministic.

brand.description: The brand slug to check against, for example magic-unicorn.

file.description: Catalog file basename to check, for example logo-wordmark.png. Provide with asset and kind.

asset.description: The asset type of the file, for example logo or og_image.

kind.description: Where the file lives: generated or imported. Defaults to generated.

text.description: A piece of copy to check for banned terms, em-dashes, and required terms. Use instead of a file for a text-only check.

tools.name: list_brand_agents
tools.description: List a brand's agent identities, newest first. An agent identity belongs to exactly one brand and inherits its voice and visual language, so any agent a company spins up (a Steward, a Specialist, or a custom agent) is on brand by construction. Each entry carries slug, name, role, bio, inherited voice tone, the avatar URL and variant state URLs, the compliance verdict, and a governance bucket. The same roster GET /api/brands/{slug}/agents serves.

tools.name: get_agent_manifest
tools.description: Get a brand agent's Brigade/suite-consumable identity manifest: the portable, machine-readable identity record other suite modules and the Brigade autonomy agents consume. Returns the schema, name, role, bio, brand, the avatar URL plus the variant state URLs and servable size derivatives, the voice tone, the brand palette, and the avatar's compliance verdict. The same document GET /api/brands/{slug}/agents/{agent}/manifest serves.

tools.name: get_agent_team
tools.description: Get a brand's agent team: the Director, the brand Steward, and its agents. A per-brand rollup. director is the single Director persona (Iris) every brand shares; steward is this brand's dedicated agent (named for the brand, its avatar the brand's canonical mark); agents is the list of created agent identities. The governance block tallies those agents by avatar compliance bucket (on_brand, needs_review, or unrated) so a view can show coverage at a glance. The same rollup GET /api/brands/{slug}/agents/team serves.

tools.name: create_agent
tools.description: Create an on-brand agent identity for a brand. The agent-facing door to spin up a Steward, a Specialist, or a custom agent that comes out on brand by construction: it belongs to the brand and inherits the brand's voice tone. The slug is derived from the name. No avatar is generated here; call generate_agent_avatar or generate_agent_variants next. A duplicate agent, an unknown brand, or a name that yields no valid slug is returned as a structured error.

name.description: The agent's display name, for example Iris.

role.description: The agent's role, for example brand steward.

bio.description: Optional short bio for the agent.

tools.name: generate_agent_avatar
tools.description: Generate an on-brand avatar for an agent, save it, and compliance-check it. Generates a single primary avatar through the same backend resolution every other on-brand image uses, saves it under the agent's directory, and runs the brand color compliance check on it (advisory; a failing check never blocks the save). Returns the refreshed identity with the avatar URL set and the compliance verdict.

tools.name: generate_agent_variants
tools.description: Generate an agent's full on-brand avatar state set and record it. Generates the whole avatar state set (primary, thinking, success, alert) as one recognizable character on brand by construction where only the expression changes, saves each (primary as avatar.png, the rest as avatar-<state>.png), compliance-checks each (advisory), and writes the variants map onto the agent while keeping the primary as the canonical avatar. Returns the refreshed identity carrying the variant state URLs.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List the in-module specialist agents (director, brand_research, brand_intake, asset_pack, avatar, brand_critic, tagger, refine) and their input contracts. The same roster GET /api/agents serves, projected from the one Brigade registry that also backs the REST surface. Each entry carries the stable name, a human description, the JSON-schema input_schema an agent payload must satisfy, the auth scopes a caller must hold, and the minimum tier. Use a name and its input_schema with run_agent.

tools.name: run_agent
tools.description: Run one specialist agent against a JSON payload and return its result. The agent-facing form of POST /api/agents/{name}/run. name is one of the specialists from list_agents; payload is that agent's input verbatim (see its input_schema). Routes through the same registry-resolved class and runner the REST route uses, with the caller's workspace threaded for best-effort spend attribution. The specialists degrade gracefully (a status like skipped or research_only) when the LLM gateway or Brigade is absent. Some agents (asset_pack, avatar) plan against the metered gateway, so a non-dry-run payload may incur spend.

name.description: The specialist agent name. See list_agents.

payload.description: The agent's input dict (its shape is per-agent; see its input_schema). Defaults to empty.

tools.name: plan_generation
tools.description: Turn a free-text generation ask into a concrete, valid GenerateRequest. The agent-facing form of POST /api/plan-generation. From a plain instruction plus any control values you know, the planner picks a brand, asset type, variant, topic, and platform from the real brand slugs and asset types this backend knows (the same workspace-scoped brand context the GUI sees), validates the pick, and returns a valid request plus a rationale and the fields it assumed. No image is generated and no spend occurs; this only plans. Degrades to a deterministic heuristic when the gateway is unavailable.

brand.description: Optional active brand slug to default to when the text is silent.

backend.description: Optional explicit backend override to keep.

annotations.title: Plan a generation from free text

tools.name: director_chat
tools.description: Talk to Iris, the brand director, and get a reply plus a routed intent. The agent-facing form of POST /api/director/chat. Iris answers in persona and classifies the turn into an intent (chat, single, pack, research, agent, compliance). For the agent and compliance intents she ACTS through the same shared flow the route uses (creating the identity, or scoring the catalog/copy), so the reply already reflects the result. Routes through the same Director flow with the caller's workspace threaded. Never fails on an LLM problem: an unreachable gateway degrades to a graceful in-persona chat reply.

message.description: The operator's new line to Iris.

brand.description: Active brand slug in the Studio, if any.

tools.name: approve_asset
tools.description: Operator override: flip an asset's lifecycle status to approved. The agent-facing form of POST /api/assets/approve, a thin alias for transition_asset with to=approved. Writes lifecycle_status=approved into the sidecar (preserving every other key) and appends an approved activity event, through the same shared boundary the REST route uses. Returns the refreshed catalog record.

asset.description: Asset type key the file lives under, for example logo.

file.description: The asset file name to approve, for example logo-wordmark.png.

kind.description: Which tree the file is in: generated (default) or imported.

tools.name: transition_asset
tools.description: Move an asset to a new lifecycle state and record it on the activity feed. The agent-facing form of POST /api/assets/transition. Locates the asset's sidecar and writes lifecycle_status=to into it, preserving every other key, then appends one activity event attributing the move to actor with an optional note. Routes through the same shared boundary the REST route and approve_asset use. to is one of needs_review, approved, changes_requested, archived.

asset.description: Asset type key the file lives under, for example logo.

file.description: The asset file name to move, for example logo-wordmark.png.

kind.description: Which tree the file is in: generated (default) or imported.

note.description: Optional human reason recorded on the activity feed.

actor.description: Who is acting (default mcp, so an agent-driven move is attributed to the MCP surface).

tools.name: upload_asset
tools.description: Bring an existing image into a brand kit's imported/ tree. The agent-facing form of POST /api/assets/upload. Supply the image either as file_path (an absolute path the server can read) or as file_base64 (the raw bytes, base64-encoded) with a filename. The bytes land under imported/<asset_type>/ with a catalog sidecar (source=upload), are compliance-stamped on landing, and come back in the same AssetRecord shape GET /api/assets serves. Routes through the same upload.save_upload core the REST route uses (same validation, same size cap, same sidecar).

brand.description: Brand slug the asset belongs to. Must exist.

asset_type.description: Asset type key the image is, for example logo. See list_asset_types.

file_path.description: Absolute path to a readable image file. Use this OR file_base64.

file_base64.description: The image bytes, base64-encoded. Use this OR file_path; when set, also pass filename.

filename.description: The file name to store under (and, for file_base64, the source of the stored extension).

content_type.description: Optional MIME type (image/png, image/jpeg, image/svg+xml, image/webp). Inferred from the filename when omitted.

variant.description: Optional variant label recorded on the asset.

annotations.title: Upload an asset into a brand kit

tools.name: update_agent
tools.description: Edit an agent's persona text (role and/or bio); avatar and voice untouched. The agent-facing form of PATCH /api/brands/{slug}/agents/{agent}. Only the fields you pass change; the avatar, voice, voice tone, and compliance are left alone. An empty role is rejected; an empty bio clears the bio. Routes through the same agent_identity layer the REST API and Studio use.

agent.description: Agent slug, for example iris. See list_brand_agents.

role.description: New role text, if changing it. An empty/whitespace role is rejected.

bio.description: New bio text, if changing it. An empty string clears the bio.

tools.name: set_agent_voice
tools.description: Bind (or clear) the agent's spoken voice from the catalog. The agent-facing form of PUT /api/brands/{slug}/agents/{agent}/voice. A non-empty voice_id must be one of the catalog voices (see list_voices); a null/empty voice_id clears the binding. The engine is resolved from the catalog when omitted. Routes through the same agent_identity layer the REST API and Studio use.

agent.description: Agent slug, for example iris. See list_brand_agents.

voice_id.description: A catalog voice id (see list_voices), or null/empty to clear.

engine.description: Optional engine override (resolved from the catalog when omitted).

speed.description: Optional speech speed multiplier recorded on the binding.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List the catalog of assignable agent voices. The same roster GET /api/voices serves: the curated TTS voices an agent can be bound to (each with id, label, engine, kind, and a short descriptor) plus whether live preview is wired. Use a voice id with set_agent_voice.

tools.name: read_activity
tools.description: Read the append-only activity / provenance feed, newest first. The agent-facing form of GET /api/activity. Returns the recent events from the on-disk feed (who did what, when, to which asset), optionally filtered to one brand slug, capped at limit. Mirrors the route's tenancy: a workspace-scoped caller sees only its own brands' events; unscoped (stdio / CLI) sees the global feed.

brand.description: Optional brand slug to filter to one brand's events.

limit.description: Max events to return, 1..500 (default 50). Out-of-range is clamped.

tools.name: get_brand_compliance
tools.description: Run the deterministic compliance check over a brand's whole catalog. The agent-facing form of GET /api/brands/{slug}/compliance. Scores every catalog asset with the same engine check_compliance uses, then rolls the verdicts into a summary (pass/warn/fail/skipped counts and an average score) plus a per-asset row list. Routes through the same shared rollup the REST route uses. No LLM and no spend.

tools.name: fetch_asset_bytes
tools.description: Fetch one catalog asset's bytes as MCP image content the agent can SEE. The agent-facing form of GET /api/assets/file, but returning native MCP image content (not a URL) so a vision-capable agent can actually view the output and judge it. Resolves brand-kits/<brand>/<kind>/<asset>/<file> and refuses anything that escapes the kits root, with the same workspace visibility guard the REST file route uses. Raster images (png/jpg/webp/gif) are returned as image content; a vector (svg) or any other type is returned as a structured error pointing at its on-disk path.

asset.description: Asset type key the file lives under, for example logo.

file.description: The asset file name, for example logo-wordmark.png.

kind.description: Which tree the file is in: generated (default) or imported.

annotations.title: Fetch asset bytes as an image

prompts.name: launch_full_brand_kit
prompts.description: Stand up a brand from a name and generate its full on-brand asset kit.

prompts.name: audit_brand_compliance
prompts.description: Audit a brand's catalog against its rules and remediate the fails.

prompts.name: stand_up_steward_agent
prompts.description: Create an on-brand steward agent for a brand and give it an avatar.
